title: 4D-STEM Angular Correlation Analysis of Amorphous SiO2/Si Interface for Spin Qubit Devices
content: Advanced quantum computing systems, particularly those based on spin qubits, are significantly affected by charge noise arising from material imperfections and structural disorder in the material stack. A critical source of this noise is the interface between amorphous SiO2 and crystalline Si, where defects and inhomogeneities influence qubit coherence. In this study, we employ four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) to investigate medium range ordering (MRO) at the SiO2/Si interface by collecting spatially resolved nanobeam electron diffraction patterns, enabling the examination of local structural variations previously inaccessible through conventional imaging methods.
